what: The element is bound straight to one stretch of the view timeline as it passes through the screen. By default, from the moment its top edge touches the bottom of the screen until its bottom edge is fully in (entry 0→100%), it goes from its starting look (pushed up −240px, .95 scale, transparent, etc. via --fx-x, --fx-y, --fx-scale, --fx-o) back to its own look, giving a parallax where photos settle later than the scroll. The out type runs in reverse, from its own look to an end look (the Hero panel turns transparent as it leaves). The slip type stays in place until 25% of the range, then slides out to the end look (400px right, transparent) by the end (the News card in the Hero corner). It is CSS ported straight from the site builder’s 「Scroll」 motion (animation-timeline: view()), so there is no JS.

options.--fx-range: view timeline ranges (via style), default entry 0% entry 100% — kept exactly as the original animation-range, like ‹entry 0% contain 100%›, ‹contain 0% exit 100%› and ‹exit 0% exit 100%›
options.--fx-x · --fx-y: Start (end for out and slip) offset (via style), default 0px
options.--fx-scale: Start scale (out·slip use end, set via style), default 1 — card .95
options.--fx-o: Initial (final for out·slip) opacity (via style), default 1
options.look: out: Morphs from its own shape to the end shape
options.look: slip: Stays in place until 25% of the range, then moves to the end shape

use: · News Card
note: Browsers without scroll timelines (some Product) don’t animate and stand in their final shape — the original STUDIO does the same if the polyfill arrives late. Used with smooth scroll (lenis) it’s a view timeline, so nothing needs separate syncing
